original.description: As part of the European Resilience from Space - Earth Observation (ERS-EO) Element 2 Programme, and in line with the Space Resilience Node (SRN) Workplan 2026 approved on 26th February 2026, ESA intends to issue a competitive tender (ERS-SRN-02) for one (1) harmonization study (up to 300k, 5 - 12 months) which will consolidate the findings from individual SRN User Needs Studies (see Tender Action 1000046333). The objective of the study is to derive or confirm common user needs and requirements for SRNs to inform the SRN Reference Framework, and to identify gaps in space-enabled products to support SRN users' public protection and disaster response activities.

original.description: Approved at CM25 under Component 3: Future PNT Demonstrators of the FutureNAV Programme, NovaMoon is a lunar-based local differential, selenodetic/geodetic and timing station that will enhance Moonlight and LunaNet lunar PNT services and support lunar scientificexperimentation.  This activity comprises Phases B/C/D/E/F of NovaMoon and is organized in three incremental builds, the development of which would allow to reach the full NovaMoon configuration (meeting all NovaMoon mission objectives) with NovaMoon Build3 aimed to fly on Argonaut2. NovaMoon Intermediate Builds1 and 2 will be designed to be as lander independent as possible (providing maximum flexibility in terms of lander opportunities). NovaMoon aims to demonstrate the following main objectives:1. Reference localPNT differential station (< 1 metre accuracy in real time),2. International Advanced "geodetic" Lunar Reference Station (< 10 cm accuracy),3. International "Lunar Time-reference" Laboratory ( ns-level).

original.description: IMPACT 10 is an ESA Earth Observation activity aimed at assessing and demonstrating the scientific and socio economic value generated by selected activities of the Earth and Mission Science Division (EOP SM). It focuses on scientific studies, mission science contributions, and programme enabling work supporting future EO missions. It also covers a new branch of "Future Science" activities. Within EOP SM, "Future Science" refers to forward looking science studies aligned with the ESA EO Science Strategy. These studies are designed to address fundamental Earth system science gaps that are not covered by current or planned missions. They therefore go beyond the scope of existing Science Plans activities. The activity will develop a robust and traceable methodology to assess both science impact and socio economic impact. Science impact will include, for example, scientific outputs, modelling advances, retrieval improvements, uncertainty characterisation, mission requirement support, community building, and uptake in international assessments. Socio economic impact will include, for example, industrial competitiveness, innovation spillovers, policy support, and broader societal and economic value.

original.description: To advance hybrid manufacturing strategies that integrate conventional and advanced techniques to enhance the performance, functionality and competitiveness of space hardware.Description:Hybrid manufacturing combines subtractive methods (e.g. milling, turning,grinding) with additive processes(e.g. powder bed processes, direct energy deposition). It may also include fabrication/joining steps like welding,bonding or brazing. This approach aims to overcome limitations of individual processes, enabling theproduction ofhigh-performance, competitive components. Such methodologies are of growing relevance particularly in propulsion, thermal management and structural systems. The key drivers include:- Geometric complexity: enabling the manufacture of intricate, topology-optimisedstructures difficult to realiseby conventional means alone.- Material efficiency: by adding material only where needed, hybrid manufacturing reduces waste and optimizes material usage.- Functional performance: enabling graded material properties, local reinforcements or tailored functionality.- Cost and lead time: consolidating steps, minimising waste and enabling complex geometries, though it mayrequire specialised planning, equipment and qualification.- Design flexibility: greater customization and flexibility in design, making it ideal for producing bespoke or low volume parts.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Survey of relevant techniques, materials and equipment capabilities relevant to a hybrid manufacturing approach.- Selection of two representative case studies with associated requirements (e.g. one propulsion component, one thermal management part).- Design and definition of the hybrid manufacturing route for each case study.- Manufacturing and functional testing of demonstrators. The utilisation of new digital methods for supportinghybrid manufacturing decisions is welcomed. This may include artificial intelligence techniques, such asdeep/federated learning techniques, as well as a focus on use-cases of generatively designed parts (whichinherently benefit from the hybrid manufacturing techniques), alongside the artificial intelligence and machine learning data-driven learning.- Economic analysis, including cost comparison with conventional approaches and life-cycle considerations.Deliverables: Breadboard, ReportNOTE: This activity is currently in the GSTP Work Plan but will only be implemented after confirmation of financial support from Delegations. The final list of participating states will be known at tender issue.

original.description: ERS-EO Proof of Concept on Critical Infrastructure ManagementThe ERS-EO Element 1 Critical Infrastructure Monitoring Prof of Concept is intended to demonstrate the step improvement for enhanced monitoring and management of critical infrastructure resulting from the effective combination of diverse EO and non-EO capabilities representative of the future Earth Observation Governmental Service (EOGS) capacity.  In particular, the customization and fusion of these capabilities will generate significant improvements in tasking response, persistent data collection, information delivery latency, expanded information content andflexibility and adaptability in response to dynamic situations. In this context, the Critical Infrastructure Monitoring PoC will:Stimulate innovative combinations of public and private EO systems to support improved and more flexible tasking, response latency, persistence and cross-operator cueing;Develop customized workflows connecting satellite operators, non-EO data providers, analytics tool developers and critical infrastructure operators to ensure enhanced capability to detect, characterize, respond to and mitigateemergent threats and anomalies;Verify the improvements achievable over current state of the art with respect to emerging threat detection and mitigation action execution for critical infrastructure operators under realistic operating conditions;With respect to gaps in current capabilities, elaborate technical approaches for their resolution, verify their impact under representative operational environments and conditionsand elaborate a road map for eventual transfer to full operations based on exclusively European technology. The contract will integrate existing EO and non-EO capabilities as well as capabilities at an advanced stage of development into a pre-operational network providing a range of analysis support information. The procurement will be structured into three periods as follows:Step[BJ1]  1:requirements consolidation and initial operating capability specification, implementation and testing.Step 2 initial capability demonstrations under realistic operating conditions covering extended routine threat mitigation, timely detection, characterization and response elaboration for emerging threats and anomaly/event response situationsStep 3: extended capability demonstration under fully representative conditions as agreed in the milestone review concluding Step 2 activities All underlying Information and Communication Technology (ICT) functions will be provided by the ERS-EO Element 1 Testbed.
